parents.rule: All prior known-truth results remain immutable.

goal: Test EOG finite-world falsification on occurrence histories generated by an independent stochastic metapopulation simulator rather than by the same EOG set/reachability code used for evaluation.

generator_independence.evaluator: EOG finite-world reconstruction is used only after synthetic observations have been generated.

associates.partner: independent stochastic metapopulation with its own A and M; final realized mask is frozen before focal simulation
associates.antagonist: independent stochastic metapopulation with its own A and M; final realized mask is frozen before focal simulation
associates.source_policy: partner source equals focal source; antagonist source lies on far-right side

focal_process.structural_truth: A × B × M defines exact zero/non-zero transitions, but occupancy within allowed structure is stochastic
focal_process.colonization: unoccupied eligible nodes colonize with probability 1-(1-beta)^k from k occupied accessible neighbors
focal_process.persistence: occupied eligible nodes persist stochastically; focal source is retained as the founding source
focal_process.observation: perfect positive occurrence detection in v3 primary experiment; absence is not used as evidence

stochastic_denominator.seed_rule: SHA-256 of scenario_id and replicate index
stochastic_denominator.design_stop_rule: Associate degeneracy or focal-source invalidity is retained as DESIGN_STOP and is not replaced.

hypotheses.claim: For every eligible stochastic run and accumulated observation horizon, the exact structural truth world is never eliminated by EOG.
Because accumulated positive occurrences only increase over time, the compatible EOG world set can only contract or remain unchanged.
hypotheses.rule: Any world-set expansion between observation horizons refutes S2.

hypotheses.claim: Any false candidate whose full structural reachable set contains the truth structural reachable set cannot be eliminated by positive-only stochastic occurrences.
hypotheses.rule: Elimination of a declared positive-superset world refutes S3.

hypotheses.claim: By horizon 40, every activated truth scenario eliminates at least one structurally under-permissive false world in at least one eligible replicate.
hypotheses.rule: A scenario with zero strict contraction across all eligible replicates refutes S4 for that scenario.

hypotheses.claim: At least one truth scenario remains non-identifiable in some eligible horizon-40 replicates despite perfect positive occurrence observation.
hypotheses.rule: If every eligible run in every scenario uniquely recovers truth, S5 is refuted.

hypotheses.claim: When truth is removed from the candidate universe, an observed stochastic occurrence set falsifies the remaining finite universe if and only if every remaining candidate has at least one observed positive witness it cannot support.
hypotheses.rule: Any mismatch between the witness criterion and empty compatible set refutes S6.

hypotheses.claim: Using the accumulated positive-occurrence history eliminates at least as many worlds as using only the final occupied snapshot, with at least one strict improvement somewhere in the frozen experiment.
hypotheses.rule: Any run where final snapshot eliminates more worlds refutes weak monotonicity; no strict improvement anywhere refutes the strict component.

claim_boundary: Generator and EOG evaluator are code-independent but share the preregistered ecological parameter semantics.
v3 does not claim the simulator is a realistic model of any named taxon.
Positive-only inference cannot use unobserved cells as absences.
Stochastic non-occurrence is not evidence against a candidate world.
A surviving world is not promoted to historical truth.

language.cxx_trigger: Only profile after the frozen v3 workload; C++ may accelerate simulation but must not change the scientific generator contract.
